narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 63.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt—roughly two chances in three. That is a risk estimate, not a certainty, but it was high enough to trigger rejection.

The strongest factor was your middle family-income bracket, which pushed the prediction toward failure; accepted students were more often from upper-middle-income families. The second strongest was your first-year academic standing: you were in the fifth decile, below the sixth-decile average among accepted students, and this also increased predicted risk. Your LSAT score of 39 was the third most influential factor and added a smaller push toward failure. Other details in your profile were not enough to offset these risks.

Next, ask admissions for a human review and for an explanation of how this prediction affected your case. Seek academic and bar-exam advising, discuss whether retaking the LSAT or strengthening your record would help, and provide context about your background and first-year performance. Also consider applying to additional schools or programs.
